hook: A paper about phone noise quietly ended up on Wall Street.

instagram.caption:
A paper about phone noise quietly ended up on Wall Street.

In 1956, John Kelly at Bell Labs asked: if a tip is only sometimes right, what fraction of your bankroll should you bet?

He maximised log-wealth, took the derivative, and got one clean answer: f* = (bp − q) / b. Bet more and you eventually go broke. Bet less and you leave growth on the table.

Ed Thorp used it — first in Vegas, then on Wall Street. Twenty percent a year for 28 years.

Save this.
